reasons: The rule constrains audit rights exercisable against us; the cited paragraphs contain no audit, inspection, records-examination or usage-verification right in Kubient's favour, so the absence is at least as protective as the preferred position.
Correctly classified as compliant rather than 'missing' — treating it as missing would require inserting an audit obligation against our own party, which the rule does not seek.
No redline and no counterparty comment were proposed, which is the expected output for a compliant finding; the rendered redline is identical to the original text.
The failed 'audit frequency limited' deterministic check is explainable heuristic noise where no audit clause exists at all, and does not evidence a gap.
Rationale accurately parks the separate (and favourable-to-us) point about Kubient-measured Impressions and revenue reporting under a different rule, avoiding double-flagging.
